title: Patch: the AI's count of a board's coming hits drops a Windfury unit's second swing once its first swing's strike back kills it, and counts a Frenzy unit's swing after each kill

**Issue #4402 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4402: Patch: the AI's count of a board's coming hits drops a Windfury unit's second swing once its first swing's strike back kills it, and counts a Frenzy unit's swing after each kill
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the computer opponent works out how much damage a board can deal to a hero in a turn, it assumes a unit that may attack twice always gets both attacks. That holds even when the first attack runs into a defender that kills the attacker back. It also never expects a unit that earns another attack by killing a defender to take that attack. Both mistakes throw its judgement badly, because it treats facing lethal as close to a lost game.

For example, with Overdrive Projector out, every unit may attack twice. An enemy 4/4 facing the AI's 4/4 Taunt reads to the AI as 'kill the Taunt, then 4 to the face', though the 4/4 dies in that trade. At 4 life the AI believes it is dead next turn, so it walls up or trades badly for nothing. The other way round, against Tmack Trav (7/7, attacks again after a kill), the AI thinks its 3/3 Taunt holds it off completely. In the game, Tmack Trav kills the Taunt, survives and hits the hero for 7. Once this is built, a practice player sees the AI read these boards the way the game plays them.

## Why

- **Windfury.** The AI's quick read of a board's coming hits is the Taunt walk behind `face_threat` and `ready_gap`. It pushes one entry per swing a unit has (`attacks_per_turn`, `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1489-1491`; `attacks_left`, `crates/ai/src/lethal.rs:165-171`) and walks those entries past the Taunts (`soak_past_taunts`, `evaluate.rs:1630`). The only attacker it ever stops is one a First Strike Taunt kills before it lands (`falls_to_first_strike`, `evaluate.rs:1937`). An attacker killed by the Taunt's simultaneous strike back (§4.3 step 2) keeps every later swing, though the engine gives a destroyed unit none (§6.1 Windfury row, R636).
- **Frenzy.** The AI reads Frenzy only as an attack hook to price (`has_attack_hook`, `evaluate.rs:520-523`). The walk never adds the swing the engine frees when an attack destroys the Unit it attacked and the attacker survives (R3543003, `crates/engine/src/combat.rs:2424-2431`; one per kill). So a Frenzy attacker's walk ends at the first Taunt it breaks.
- **These reads carry weight.**
  - `evaluate` charges `lethal_threat` (150) once the enemy's read reaches the seat's life, against `threat_per_damage` (0.4) per point below that line. It adds `lethal_on_board` or `lethal_pressure` for its own read (`evaluate.rs:3256-3280`; `crates/ai/src/config.rs:788-793`).
  - `wall_switches_priced` decides whether to wall from the same read (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:1162-1181`).
  - `ready_gap` puts the hero hits first in the move order and gates the reply's walls (`candidates.rs:1047`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs:704`).
  - The Duos pool loss reads it as well (`crates/ai/src/duos.rs:146`).
  - The lethal solver, the reply's trades and the beam play attacks through `reduce` and already get this right. Only the static count is wrong.
- **The cards that deal these boards.**
  - Overdrive Projector and Overdrive Dome give every Unit on both sides Windfury, and Surge Alloy gives one Unit Windfury.
  - Rampaging Rhino, Windfast (with its Windfurious Prime) and Servo Surge are printed with Windfury and without Ranged.
  - Ranged Windfury units such as Duo, Spectre and Reign take no strike back from a non-Ranged Taunt (R783000), so they rightly keep both swings.
  - Tmack Trav and the Classic Golem token have Frenzy, and Graphite grants it.
  - Windfury and Frenzy are both in the random combat keyword pool that Plastic Surgery, Zao Gao, Keymaster Keenus, After Burner and the Conjure Rush Tokens draw from (§6, the random keyword pool).
- **Same kind of fix as before.** The walk got the same treatment for Frozen and summoning-sick units (#4170), Scorch and Toxopid (#3909), Brittle (#3793) and Cleave through a GIGA (#4257). Neither the README nor any test says that multi-swing is left out on purpose. `crates/ai/tests/ai/evaluate.rs:477` and `crates/ai/tests/ai/lethal.rs:483` only check that a Windfury unit with a free path counts twice.

## Proposal

1. **Drop a dead attacker's later swings.** In the walk (`soak_past_taunts` and its callers), track each attacker by instance. Read a hit's strike back the way `falls_to_first_strike` reads a First Strike one, but for §4.3 step 2. That covers Divine Shield, Armor unless the Taunt pierces, the attacker's own cap, Indestructible, Poisonous, the exile read, Ranged's exemption and the pools. When the attacker does not survive it, the hit still lands, but every later swing of that attacker is dropped, whether it waits at a Taunt or is free for the hero. A Windfury attacker's second swing starts from the damage its first strike back left.
2. **Give Frenzy its swing.** When an attacker's hit destroys the Taunt it attacked and the attacker survives the strike back, a Frenzy attacker gets one more swing. Poisonous and exile kills count; a Cleave neighbour's death does not. The new swing carries the entry's own hero permission, so a Rush unit that entered this turn still may not hit the hero. It applies once per such kill.
3. **Put both behind one flag** in `EvalWeights`, on in `AI_EVAL` and off in `GREEDY_EVAL`, as `frozen_sick_before_swing` and `giga_cleave_read` are, so the gates' frozen yardstick does not move. `face_threat` and `ready_gap` both get the change through `damage_past_taunts`. The walk's existing orders stay as they are: smallest first, breaker first and Cleave first, with the larger result counting.
4. **Screen it** on improve-dev against the control as `training/improve.md` (A screen) says. Record the result in the flag's config comment, inconclusive or not.
5. **Document it.** Add the rule to `crates/ai/README.md` beside the other walk reads. Add a ruling note in the issue's block, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`: `soak_past_taunts`, a strike-back reader beside `falls_to_first_strike`, and `face_threat_from`'s entries
- `crates/ai/src/config.rs`: the flag in `EvalWeights`, `AI_EVAL` and `GREEDY_EVAL`
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/`: a new test file listed in `mod.rs`
- `crates/ai/README.md`, `spec/rulings/R<issue>000.md`, `spec/pending/<issue>.md`
- SPEC §4.3, §6.1's Windfury and Frenzy rows, §9.9; R636, R3543003, R783000

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With every Unit Windfury (an Overdrive Projector awake), an enemy 4/4 against the seat's 4/4 with Taunt in Attack Position, and nothing else on the board, reads 0 damage to the seat's hero in `face_threat`. With the enemy unit at 4/5 it reads 4.
- [ ] A Ranged Windfury attacker against a non-Ranged Taunt it destroys still reads its second swing on the hero.
- [ ] A Tmack Trav that did not enter this turn reads 7 on the hero against a 3/3 Taunt, and 0 against a 7/3 Taunt whose strike back destroys it. A Taunt that dies only to a Cleave splash (Cleave granted) frees no swing.
- [ ] A Frenzy attacker that breaks two Taunts in turn, surviving both, reads one swing on the hero after the second.
- [ ] Each board above is also played out through `reduce` in its test, making the attacks the read assumes in its order. The hero damage the engine deals equals the read.
- [ ] On the seat's own turn, `ready_gap` gives the gap the engine allows on the Windfury and Frenzy boards.
- [ ] A test holds `GREEDY_EVAL`'s read of every board above to the old read.
- [ ] The flag's comment in `config.rs` records the improve-dev screen, with its interval and its decided and diverged counts.
- [ ] These pass: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh gate` and `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Size and risks

- **Size:** about 100 to 200 lines in one crate, plus tests. It is `difficulty:hard` under CLAUDE.md rule 11, since it changes the AI's evaluation.
- **The screen will probably be inconclusive.** These boards are uncommon. The protocol then has the scene tests settle the change and the config comment record the screen (`training/improve.md`, A screen, step 3).
- **Pinned decisions may move.** Other AI tests whose boards hold one of these keywords may change their pinned decision. Each moved decision needs a stated reason, not a retune.
- **Attack order.** A different order of attacks could keep a swing that smallest-first now drops. The walk already takes the larger of its orders.
- **Feature values move.** `features.rs` reads `face_threat` for the rows `positions` writes, so those values change on these boards while the layout stays the same. The builder checks `FEATURES_VERSION`'s rule.
- **Speed:** the walk gains one strike-back check per hit, a few comparisons, so decision time does not move measurably.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44933454154)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Make the AI's static Taunt walk (`soak_past_taunts`, `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`) read §4.3 step 2: an attacker destroyed by a Taunt's simultaneous strike back lands its hit but loses every later swing, and a Frenzy attacker that destroys its target and survives gains one more swing. Both sit behind one new `EvalWeights` flag, on in `AI_EVAL`, off in `GREEDY_EVAL`, so `face_threat`, `ready_gap`, `wall_switches_priced` and the Duos pool loss all follow with no changes of their own. One correction to the proposal: exile kills must **not** free a Frenzy swing — the engine grants Frenzy only on `Destroyed` events and an exiled unit has none (`combat.rs:116`, §4.5 step 1, R1124).

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs` | change | `soak_past_taunts`: dead-attacker tracking, wound tracking, Frenzy extra swing; new `survives_strike_back` beside `falls_to_first_strike`; doc updates on `face_threat_from`, `damage_past_taunts_with` |
| `crates/ai/src/config.rs` | change | `EvalWeights.strike_back_survival_read` + doc, `AI_EVAL` on, `GREEDY_EVAL` off + list comment, screen record |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/strike_back_survival.rs` | new | `r4402000_*` scene + engine-parity + GREEDY + `ready_gap` tests |
| `crates/ai/tests/ai/mod.rs` | change | add `pub mod strike_back_survival;` |
| `crates/ai/README.md` | change | one walk paragraph after the `giga_cleave_read` paragraph |
| `spec/rulings/R4402000.md` | new | ruling note (R4402000 verified free: only `R4154402.md` matches `grep 4402`) |
| `spec/pending/4402.md` | new | §11 paragraph |
| `spec/06-keywords.md` | change | append `[[R4402000]]` to Windfury row 59 and Frenzy row 60 |
| `spec/09-architecture.md` | change | append `[[R4402000]]` to the Evaluation face-damage sentence |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`, `spec/CARDS.md`, or any other crate or app.

## Steps

1. Re-read the governing text: spec §4.3 steps 1–2, §4.4 steps 1–4 and 7, §4.5 step 1, §6.1 Windfury/Frenzy rows, §9.9 Evaluation; `R636`, `R3543003`, `R783000`; `falls_to_first_strike` (`evaluate.rs:1937`) as the pattern to copy; `combat.rs` `takes_strike_back` (883), First-Strike ordering in `resolve_combat`, and Frenzy's `destroyed_ids` condition (`combat.rs:2424-2431`).
2. `config.rs`: add `pub strike_back_survival_read: bool` to `EvalWeights` directly after `giga_cleave_read`, with a doc comment in the sibling style (ruling id, what the walk does, off-behavior, screen record added in step 8). Set `true` in `AI_EVAL`, `false` in `GREEDY_EVAL`, and add it to `GREEDY_EVAL`'s "is off" flag list.
3. `evaluate.rs`: add `survives_strike_back(state, attacker, wounds, stand, pools, w) -> bool` directly after `falls_to_first_strike`, mirroring its bespoke §4.4 math against the attacker's tracked `(shield, health)`: `!takes_strike_back` reads true (R783000); attacker First Strike vs non-First-Strike Taunt whose hit destroys it reads true (no strike back); else Divine Shield pops, Armor unless the Taunt pierces (R346), own cap (R2179005), Indestructible reads true, Poisonous or `exiles_what_it_damages` (by `w`) reads false, `pools.attacker` soaks fresh as the sibling does, a converting Taunt reads true (R4064001).
4. `evaluate.rs` `soak_past_taunts`, all gated on `w.strike_back_survival_read`: track `wounds: IndexMap<String, (bool, i32)>` per attacker id seeded lazily from `unit_view`, and `dead: IndexSet<String>` (both types already imported). For every bound hit that is not First-Strike-killed and not deferred to `stopped` (shield-pops and Armor-absorbed hits included — the simultaneous step still answers them), run step 3; on death record the id but still process the hit (R59: both hits land first). Skip dead ids at the hit-loop top, in `unbound.extend(bound.filter(...))`, and in the final hero loop, so later swings die at Taunts and at the hero alike.
5. Same function: when the direct hit fells stand `i` (`health <= 0` or `poisoned`, and not `exiled`, and the stand is not Indestructible per R46) and the attacker survives per step 3 and `unit_has(state, attacker, KeywordKind::Frenzy)`, push one `(attacker, attack, may_hit_hero)` entry into `unbound` before its sort — the entry's own hero permission, so a sick Rush unit's extra swing still cannot hit the hero. Credit this before the `reborn_body` swap (a destroyed-then-returned Taunt still counts, it was destroyed). Cleave-splash kills of later stands never credit (the engine requires `destroyed_ids` to contain the attacked target).
6. Docs: one sentence each on `face_threat_from` and `damage_past_taunts_with` naming the flag; `crates/ai/README.md` paragraph after the `giga_cleave_read` one, ending "off in `GREEDY_EVAL`"; `[[R4402000]]` links on the two keyword rows and the §9.9 face-damage sentence.
7. Ruling `spec/rulings/R4402000.md` in `R4257000.md`'s shape (rule, issue board, on/off, Hearthstone line, Rejected, Not modelled, purity line), `cards` naming `§4.3, §4.4, §6.1, §9.9, R636, R3543003, R783000, R3937000`, `proven_in` naming the new test file; `spec/pending/4402.md` with the §11 paragraph in `4382.md`'s style.
8. Screen once on improve-dev: build the control from the committed tip, run `cargo jackioh arena --a self --b bin:~/control-jackioh --set improve-dev` (400 games), and write the result into the flag's `config.rs` comment in the sibling format (interval, decided `wonBoth–lostBoth`, diverged; `inconclusive (R4319000)` if so, when scene tests settle it per `training/improve.md` A-screen step 3).
9. Write the tests in §Tests, then run them plus `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh spec check`, and `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke). No web files change, so no web tests.

## Tests

All in `crates/ai/tests/ai/strike_back_survival.rs`, using `scenario`, `act` (reduce), `grant` for keywords, and `face_threat` / `face_threat_with(..., &GREEDY_EVAL)` / `ready_gap` (patterns: `cleave.rs`, `lethal.rs:47-140`). The awake-Projector board: place `stinkyscapeplus-062` face-up in backrow, clear `slumber` via `find_instance_mut`, guard-assert Windfury on both units through `unit_view`.

- `r4402000_windfury_trade_reads_zero`: projector awake; enemy `core-008` 4/4 vs seat `core-008` + granted Taunt. `face_threat` 0. Play out via `act`: attack the Taunt, both die, hero unchanged.
- `r4402000_windfury_survivor_keeps_second_swing`: same aura; enemy `core-030` Archivist 4/5 vs 4/4 Taunt. Reads 4. Play out: attack Taunt (survives at 1), attack hero (−4).
- `r4402000_ranged_windfury_keeps_both_swings`: `core-008` + granted Ranged and Windfury vs `classicplus-026` Tommy Tempo 3/3 Taunt. Reads 4; play out both swings.
- `r4402000_frenzy_extra_swing_after_survived_kill`: `stinkyscape-094` Tmack Trav 7/7 vs Tommy Tempo. Reads 7; play out kill then hero (−7).
- `r4402000_frenzy_no_swing_when_strike_back_kills`: Tmack vs `core-052` Silly Silas 7/7 + granted Taunt (no printed 7/3 Taunt exists in the catalog; 7/7 preserves the mechanic: mutual destruction). Reads 0; play out, hero unchanged. Name the substitution in a comment.
- `r4402000_frenzy_chains_across_two_taunts`: Tmack vs two Tommys. Reads 7; play out three attacks; hero −7.
- `r4402000_cleave_splash_kill_frees_no_swing`: `core-008` + granted Frenzy and Cleave attacks `stinkyscapeplus-065` Thorium Wall (0/10 Taunt) beside a Tommy; splash kills Tommy, Wall survives. Reads 0; play out; no second attack is legal. Plus a positive control in the same test: `core-008` + granted Frenzy alone vs Tommy reads 4 (proves granted Frenzy reads).
- `r4402000_greedy_keeps_old_read`: `GREEDY_EVAL` reads 4 on the `r4402000_windfury_trade` board (both swings counted) and 0 on the Tmack-vs-Tommy board (no Frenzy read).
- `r4402000_ready_gap_matches_engine`: on the seat's own turn, `ready_gap` equals the engine-allowed gap on the Windfury-trade board (0 past Taunts) and the Tmack-vs-Tommy board (7 past the Taunt); play each line out and assert the hero damage matches.

## Done when

- [ ] Every acceptance board reads as specified (0 / 4 / 7 / 0, two-Taunt chain 7, splash-only 0), each played out through `reduce` with the read's attack order and matching hero damage.
- [ ] `ready_gap` matches the engine on the seat's own turn for the Windfury and Frenzy boards.
- [ ] `GREEDY_EVAL` holds the old reads on every board above.
- [ ] Config comment records the improve-dev screen with interval, decided and diverged counts.
- [ ] Ruling note, `spec/pending/4402.md`, keyword-row and §9.9 links, README paragraph all present.
- [ ] These pass: `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo jackioh gate`, `cargo jackioh spec check`. Any moved AI pin gets a stated reason, never a retune.
- [ ] `FEATURES_VERSION` unbumped only after confirming via `git log` that prior walk-read changes (e.g. `giga_cleave_read`) did not bump it: the layout is unchanged, only the values in the existing `face_threat` field move.

## Risks

- Exile over-crediting: the proposal says exile kills free a swing, but the engine never emits `Destroyed` for an exiled unit, so Frenzy cannot trigger — crediting it would make the read disagree with `reduce` play-outs. Step 5 excludes exile; the splash test plus a Banisher-adjacent play-out would catch a regression.
- Indestructible + Poisonous: a poisoned Indestructible Taunt is spared (R46), so no Frenzy — step 5's `!Indestructible` gate. The walk's existing habit of freeing waiters on such a stand is left alone.
- Attack order: a different order could keep a swing smallest-first drops; the walk already takes the larger of its orders, and the steps keep all three orders as they are.
- Moved pins: other AI tests on Windfury/Frenzy boards may shift pinned decisions or feature values; each needs a stated reason. Decision time should not move measurably (one strike-back check per hit).

## Open questions

None for a person. The one judgment call the task left open (exile freeing a Frenzy swing) is settled by the spec and engine in favor of not crediting it, with the reason recorded above and in the ruling note's Rejected section.
```
